title: A proper generically finite map is finite near a point of local dimension at most one
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $x\in X$. Assume the local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] of Krull dimension at most $1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Assume that for every generic point $\eta$ of an irreducible component of $Y$ [def-sc-generic-point, def-weil-irreducible-components], the induced residue field extension $\kappa(f(\eta))\subseteq\kappa(\eta)$ is algebraic, meaning every element satisfies a nonzero polynomial over the smaller field [def-weil-residue-field]. Then there is an open neighbourhood $V\subseteq X$ of $x$ such that $f^{-1}(V)\to V$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

proof.text: Properness includes finite type, and finite type includes locally of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Apply [lem-per-generically-finite-quasifinite-over-dimension-one] with $g=f$, $Z=Y$, $S=X$, and $s=x$. Its local Noetherian, dimension, and generic algebraicity hypotheses are precisely the hypotheses of the item. Hence $f$ is quasi-finite at every point over $x$.

Put $F=Y\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$, the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Its underlying space is homeomorphic to $f^{-1}(\{x\})$. For every point $y$ over $x$, [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-at-point-isolated] applies because $f$ is locally of finite type and is quasi-finite at $y$. Thus each corresponding singleton of $F$ is open: $F$ is discrete.

The morphism $F\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ is the base change of $f$, hence proper by clause (1) of [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. The target is affine by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Applying [pqf-lem-proper-basic] to this proper morphism over an affine target shows that $F$ is quasi-compact.

By [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], the open covering of $F$ by all its singletons admits a finite subcover. A union of finitely many singletons is finite, so $F$ has finitely many points. The homeomorphism of [def-pc-scheme-fibre] then shows that $f^{-1}(\{x\})$ is a finite set. This also includes the empty-fibre case, using the empty finite subcover.

Apply [lem-trf-proper-finite-fibre-finite-near] to the original proper morphism $f:Y\to X$ and the point $x$. The preceding step supplies exactly its finite-set hypothesis; this theorem imposes no Noetherian condition on the target. It gives an open neighbourhood $V$ of $x$ such that $f^{-1}(V)\to V$ is finite, as required.

tool_uses.why: The pointwise quasi-finiteness-to-isolated-fibre-point implication is a generic scheme-theoretic tool, not given by this perverse-sheaf unit.
Properness of the scheme-theoretic fibre is the base-change permanence tool; this unit does not reprove it.
Quasi-compactness of a proper scheme over an affine base is a generic tool needed for the singleton-cover argument.
The general proper finite-fibre neighbourhood theorem is the final tool explicitly invoked by Tag 0AB7, using its non-Noetherian generalization Tag 02UP.
